raw_segments.text: Chorus, woe, woe, woe, let the teardrop fall,
plashing on the ground where our lord lies low.
Fall and cleanse away the cursed libation stain,
shed on this grave mound, fenced wherein together,
gifts of good or bane from the dead are found.
Lord of Argus, harken, though around the darkened mist of death and hell,
arise and hear, harken and awaken to our cry of woe,
who with might of spear shall our home deliver,
who like Aries bend until it quiver, bend the northern bow.
Who with hand upon the hilt himself will thrust with glaive,
